clue.text: Open-minded about Turner's visual imperfection

parts.note: someone open-minded is impartial, unbiased, standing aloof from the argument
RE is the Latin-derived 'regarding', about
Tina Turner, the singer

explanation.surface: An unprejudiced viewer comments on the flaws in a painting by J. M. W. Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter, which suits 'visual', but it is the singer Tina Turner.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical condition in which the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye comes away, damaging sight.

clue.text: Lower classes may get over greasy spoon in coffee

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting over another means it comes first

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification of occupations
a cheap British cafe, informally a caff

explanation.surface: Working-class customers might down a cup of coffee in a cheap cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'greasy spoon' or CAFF is a cheap, no-frills British cafe serving fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal name for decaffeinated coffee, the drink with its caffeine removed.

clue.text: Kind offer

definitions.meaning: to put forward formally, as a bid or a resignation

explanation.surface: A generous proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both an adjective meaning gentle and caring, and a verb meaning to present a bid or payment.

clue.text: Trial resulting from swimmer's bottom being exposed in changing cubicle

indicators.note: the letters are being changed into a new order, with a pun on a changing room
the bottom of a word is its final letter, here of the swimmer

explanation.surface: A swimmer suffers the ordeal of having their backside on show in the changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimmer's last letter is added to CUBICLE and the whole lot rearranged; 'being exposed in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a severe test or ordeal, like the vessel that holds metal in a furnace.

clue.text: Cupid's preference for alfresco libidinous conclusions

indicators.note: the conclusions of the four words are their final letters

explanation.surface: The god of love apparently likes his lustful affairs to end outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek god of love, the counterpart of the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: See 1
Milk and old Viennese cake unfinished

parts.note: EX is a prefix for former, old

indicators.note: the cake loses its final letter

parts.note: a torte is a rich layered cake typical of Vienna

explanation.surface: A cafe order: some milk and a stale Viennese pastry left half eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk someone is to exploit them and squeeze money out of them.

clue.text: Start off clear from criticism producing show

indicators.note: the start of the word is taken off

parts.note: to vindicate is to clear of blame

explanation.surface: A performer begins by shaking off bad reviews and puts on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to point out or demonstrate something.

clue.text: Endorsement is commercial choice

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: A celebrity endorsement is a deliberate marketing decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking up a policy or idea is endorsing it; synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Bamboozle angry man such as Paul Daniels?

parts.note: to con is to trick or bamboozle
from the film Twelve Angry Men, about a jury

explanation.surface: A magician who fools his audience is called an irate fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Daniels was a famous British TV magician; the question mark marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician or illusionist, of whom the television entertainer is one example.

clue.text: Film company boss's single Oscar

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob on a surface
I is the Roman numeral one
O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A movie company chief has won just one Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not a manager but a decorative knob, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood film companies are known collectively and individually as studios.

clue.text: Dave's old china holding occasional balti or wine

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: china is rhyming slang (china plate) for mate; Dave's mate is Chas, of the duo Chas and Dave

indicators.note: only every other letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An old friend nurses a curry or a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Chas and Dave were a London pub-rock duo; 'china' is rhyming slang for mate. Occasional letters of BALTI give BLI.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry white wine from the region around the Burgundy town of that name.

clue.text: Diet of junk causing a rotten smell

indicators.note: junk as a verb, to scrap, signals the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Living on junk food leaves you with bad breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinking, having an offensive smell like something rotting.

clue.text: No 2 could be

parts.note: No is an abbreviation of number, a shortened word, and 2-down's answer is a cut of meat too

explanation.surface: A remark about item number two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' is the clipped form of 'number', so it is itself an abbreviated form; 2-down (tender) can also be a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviation or quicker route; 'No' is a clipped form of a longer word.

clue.text: Meagre second crop before end of season — why, you may ask

parts.note: a craw is a bird's crop, the pouch in its gullet

indicators.note: the final letter of the word
said aloud, the question word is the letter Y

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Y

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders why the second harvest of the year was so poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' is not a harvest but the bird's gullet pouch, CRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin and bony, lean, like a meagre scrap of a creature.

clue.text: Oik catching a cold taking old ineffective remedy

indicators.note: the first piece catches the next inside it

parts.note: a pleb, an uncouth commoner
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A lout who has caught a cold takes some outdated medicine that does nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oik' is British slang for a crude, uncultured person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill with no active ingredient, given for its psychological effect.

clue.text: Rose oil left from bingo

indicators.note: the letter is taken away from the game's name

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: Perfume remains from a bingo night.
explanation.definitionFit: Variant of attar, the fragrant essential oil distilled from roses.

clue.text: Anonymous worker's scoffing drove one away

indicators.note: eating up, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: a worker bee
sent, as in drove someone mad

explanation.surface: An unnamed employee's binge eating drove a colleague off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone missing, not present where expected, such as at work or school.

clue.text: Square 50s retro style about buggy

indicators.note: styling the letters puts them into a new shape

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, so two fifties are two Ls

explanation.surface: A conventional pram designed in 1950s retro fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is just a link, as in 'a buggy is what this is about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushchair for a small child, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Perfectionist succeeded with puzzle

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
a tickler is a puzzling problem, as in brain-tickler

explanation.surface: A meticulous person managed to finish a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists on precise detail, a fusspot for exact standards.

clue.text: Paddy appearing in revival of 'Separate Tables'

indicators.note: a revival sends the letters back the other way
the letters appear inside the play's title

explanation.surface: An Irish actor is cast in a new production of Terence Rattigan's play.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like an Irishman's name but means a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British words for a fit of temper or rage, as in 'in a paddy'.

clue.text: Save one's thanks for person serving 1 Down?

parts.note: save meaning except, as does bar
one is I, and the 's stands for 'is'
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A tip-saver keeps a single thank-you for whoever brings the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee-shop worker who makes and serves espresso drinks, such as the decaf of 1 Down.

clue.text: Sovereign decree

definitions.meaning: reigning, as an adjective for the governing power

explanation.surface: A royal proclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means reigning or dominant; as a noun, an authoritative decision by a court or official.

clue.text: Spoil rascal's demeanour

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal
an air is a manner or demeanour

explanation.surface: A naughty child's attitude ruins things.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to damage, weaken or make worse.

clue.text: Lay to rest some alien Tom Baker characters

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used
letters, a run of the phrase's characters

explanation.surface: Bury some extraterrestrial villains from Tom Baker's Doctor Who days.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Baker played the Doctor in Doctor Who, so 'alien characters' suggests the monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a body in a tomb, to bury.

clue.text: Well-spoken former 'Top Gear' presenter hailed in E3?

indicators.note: E3 is an East London postcode, so the greeting is said in a Cockney accent

parts.note: Quentin Willson, an early presenter of the BBC car show, greeted with hello

explanation.surface: An articulate ex-presenter of the car programme is greeted in an East End district.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney drops the H and swallows the final syllable: ''Ello Quent'' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent and persuasive in speech, articulate.

clue.text: Intelligence of current university fellows

parts.note: AC is alternating current
fellows are men

explanation.surface: The brainpower of today's college dons.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewdness, keen insight; sharp intelligence in judgment.

clue.text: Ogle women during intermission

indicators.note: one piece falls during the other, inside it

parts.note: a gap, a break

explanation.surface: Eyeing up the ladies in the theatre interval.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to stare openly and stupidly; a British informal word.

clue.text: End of engagement like a bad movie

indicators.note: the final letter of the word
bad letters are in a mangled order

explanation.surface: A broken engagement is like a bad film.
explanation.definitionFit: An early film with a soundtrack, a picture that talks.

clue.text: No positives to appalling cocktail with last of limoncello liqueur

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed
there are to be none of the named letters left

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for positive, so positives are two Ps

indicators.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A drinker dismisses an awful cocktail mixed with a dash of lemon liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden Italian herb liqueur, used in a Harvey Wallbanger.

clue.text: Hack off a green monstrosity

indicators.note: a monstrous form of the letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: An ugly green eyesore annoys people.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British 'hack off' means to annoy, and this verb means to make furious.

clue.text: Runny brie grocer first cut to serve at barbecue

indicators.note: first tells us the shop's name is placed at the front, ahead of the cheese letters

parts.note: Spar is a chain of grocery shops

indicators.note: runny cheese loses its shape, so the letters shift

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper first cuts some runny brie to serve at a cookout.
